components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; background: var(--green, #0fb36a); color: #fff; padding: 14px 26px; border: none; border-radius: 999px; font-family: Poppins, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px; box-shadow: 0 14px 30px rgba(15,179,106,0.3); cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1), box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 18px 36px rgba(15,179,106,0.4); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(-1px) scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(15,179,106,0.4); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: SOSAN's visual system exists to connect two shores — a patient in Cameroon and a relative sending support from abroad — and make both feel equally at home on arrival. Vital Green is health and action; Trust Navy is the steady authority underneath. Warmth comes from whitespace, soft rounded surfaces, and a human voice — never from a warm-tinted background. The register is brand: the page walks a visitor up the belief ladder (legitimate → relevant → transparent → easy) before it asks for the install, so the system is built for reassurance first — low density, confident-not-shouting headings, proof given room to breathe, and disciplined motion that respects reduced-motion.
keyCharacteristics: Clean white ground; green and navy do the talking.
Two-audience equality baked into copy and imagery (patient + diaspora).
Soft, tactile, rounded surfaces — approachable, never sterile.
Trust before pitch: proof and transparency lead, the CTA follows.

rules.name: The Vital-Green Restraint Rule
rules.body: Green is action and health, not wallpaper. It carries CTAs, accents, icon marks, and confirmations — never a large reading surface. Saturated grounds are Trust Navy, not green.

rules.name: The Clean-Ground Rule
rules.body: The body background is true white (#ffffff), never a warm cream/sand/paper tint. Warmth comes from voice, spacing, and imagery.

rules.name: The Two-Job Rule
rules.body: Poppins never sets a paragraph; Inter never sets a display heading. The contrast between the families is the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Eyebrow-Budget Rule
rules.body: The uppercase tracked eyebrow is seasoning, not scaffolding. Name a section's theme with it; never reflex it above every block.

rules.name: The Tinted-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is tinted navy for neutral surfaces or green under green CTAs. Pure-black shadows are prohibited.

dos: Do lead every section with proof or transparency before the ask — walk the belief ladder, never pitch first.
Do keep body text at Ink (#16283a) or Muted (#4c5b6a) for ≥4.5:1 on white; bump toward Ink whenever contrast is close.
Do reserve full-pill (999px) for buttons, tags, and badges; keep cards at 16–26px.
Do tint every shadow navy or green — never pure black.
Do address the patient-at-home and the relative-abroad as equals in copy and imagery.
Do keep the ground true white; carry warmth through voice, spacing, and photography.
donts: Don't drift toward a cold, corporate hospital or insurance look — sterile stock and institutional blandness kill trust here.
Don't adopt a flashy startup / crypto aesthetic — no neon gradients, no hype.
Don't build a cluttered, ad-heavy portal — no dense, banner-stuffed layouts.
Don't ship the generic SaaS gradient template that could belong to any product.
Don't use gradient text or side-stripe borders (colored border-left/right > 1px) anywhere.
Don't over-round: no card, section, or input past 26px radius.
Don't let Vital Green fill a large reading surface — it is an accent and action color.
Don't set body-length text in Muted Faint (#7a8896); it fails 4.5:1 and is for decorative meta only.
